takeaway: Public reviews and internal tickets agree that large workspaces grind to a halt — the one issue both sides name. Offline remains a loud public complaint with no ticket trail; SSO is the inverse, a quiet enterprise blocker the open web never sees.

issues.title: Large workspaces get slow
issues.gist: Load lag and laggy typing once a workspace passes a few thousand pages.

evidence.quote: painfully slow to load and even typing lags
DB with 8k rows takes 12s to open

issues.title: SSO is a renewal blocker
issues.gist: Security teams will not renew without SAML; three accounts named it this quarter.

evidence.quote: no SSO/SAML is now a hard compliance blocker
asked for SSO this quarter, same driver

issues.title: Offline mode is unreliable
issues.gist: Edits lost without a connection; the top public reason power users leave.
issues.prevalence: many public reports, none in this paste

issues.title: AI add-on feels like nickel-and-diming
issues.gist: Paid users resent a second per-seat charge for AI when rivals bundle it.

love: Flexibility — one tool for notes, wikis, and databases

actions.action: Set a per-page load-time budget and ship incremental rendering for large databases
actions.why: The only issue both public reviews and internal tickets name — a retention risk on the accounts that pay.

actions.action: Ship SAML/SSO on the enterprise plan this quarter
actions.why: Quiet in public, loud in the paste: a $400K renewal is blocked. First-party-only is the signal the open web missed.

actions.action: Treat offline as a public-only ceiling until tickets confirm it
actions.why: Loud on Trustpilot, absent from this paste — verify against first-party data before staffing it as a P0.

actions.action: Weigh bundling a baseline AI allowance into paid tiers
actions.why: Intentional tradeoff owned by Leadership; public-only, so prevalence is a ceiling.
